messages.content:
You are writing for a bank's internal auditor, in UK English.
For each finding, write 2-3 plain sentences: what is wrong, why it matters, what to do.
Use ONLY the numbers given. Do not add, round, combine or calculate numbers.
Do not name customers. Return JSON: {"findings": {"<id>": "<text>", ...}}

{"CV1": "Cash deposits (in) are not monitored at all. 0% monitored: £426,953,352 across 107,723 transactions. No rule can fire on cash deposits (in), so £426,953,352 from 5,623 customers was never checked. Suggested fix: Add scenarios for cash deposits (in), including amount, frequency and split-deposit patterns.", "CV2": "Wires (in) are not monitored at all. 0% monitored: £287,038,321 across 6,899 transactions. No rule can fire on wires (in), so £287,038,321 from 1,023 customers was never checked. Suggested fix: Add scenarios for wires (in), including amount, frequency and split-deposit patterns.", "CV3": "Money order deposits (in) are not monitored at all. 0% monitored: £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions. No rule can fire on money order deposits (in), so £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers was never checked. Suggested fix: Add scenarios for money order deposits (in), including amount, frequency and split-deposit patterns.", "AD1": "Advisory pattern not caught: Multiple credit card repayments to many individuals. 25 customers match; 12% have a case; £2,115,842. The advisory warns: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\". 25 customers match this pattern, but only a transaction-count rule can see them, so only 3 have a case. Assumption: Three‑month window interpreted as 90 days; ten distinct cardholders required; amount range taken from advisory Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: multiple credit card repayments to many individuals (red flag: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\").", "AD2": "Advisory pattern not caught: Multiple money orders deposited same day below £2,500. 25 customers match; 8% have a case; £668,454. The advisory warns: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\". 25 customers match this pattern, but no rule can see these transactions, so only 2 have a case. Assumption: ‘Several’ taken as at least 2 money orders; combined total must be <£2,500; repeated on at least 2 separate days Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: multiple money orders deposited same day below £2,500 (red flag: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\").", "BL1": "50 customers with no case look highly unusual. top 50 of 43,927 unflagged customers. These customers never reached the alarm level, but their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Top reasons: 9541415110: money in (£) 607,808 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 607,808 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 17 (top 0.7% of customers) | 6334452196: money in (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 22 (top 0.5% of customers) | 6976851439: money in (£) 757,793 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 757,793 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 21 (top 0.5% of customers) Suggested fix: Send these customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.", "BL2": "Customers just under the threshold look riskier than those just over it. scores 32-39: 1.8% highly unusual vs 40-48: 0.4%. The threshold of 40 points cuts off customers who look more suspicious than many it lets through. Suggested fix: Lower the case threshold or sample scores 32-39 for review every month.", "BL3": "The valued-client list hides highly unusual customers. 19 of 25 suppressed customers in the top 2% most unusual. These customers are on the valued-client list, so they can never get a case whatever they score, and their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. 2 of them have already scored enough for a case. Suggested fix: Remove automatic suppression; review valued clients like anyone else.", "CV4": "Credit card repayments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only M03_outbound_velocity: £63,913,161. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card repayments (out).", "CA1": "Weak rule over-weighted: M01_outbound_high_risk. 5 pts, right 5.1% of the time (4-6%, n=2379). Outgoing wire or cross-border payment to a high-risk country. Only 5% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 5 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower M01_outbound_high_risk from 5 to about 2 points to cut false alarms.", "CA2": "Weak rule over-weighted: M02_large_outbound. 5 pts, right 5.5% of the time (5-6%, n=5418). Outgoing payment of £20,000 or more. Only 5% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 5 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower M02_large_outbound from 5 to about 2 points to cut false alarms.", "CA3": "Weak rule over-weighted: M03_outbound_velocity. 10 pts, right 10.1% of the time (9-11%, n=2881). 25 or more outgoing payments in a 30-day period. Only 10% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 10 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower M03_outbound_velocity from 10 to about 4 points to cut false alarms."}

reply: {"findings":{"CV1":"Cash deposits into the bank are not monitored – 0 % of £426,953,352 across 107,723 transactions were checked. As a result, £426,953,352 from 5,623 customers has never been screened, exposing the bank to undetected illicit activity. Add monitoring scenarios for cash deposits, covering amount, frequency and split‑deposit patterns.","CV2":"Wires into the bank are not monitored – 0 % of £287,038,321 across 6,899 transactions were checked. Consequently, £287,038,321 from 1,023 customers has not been examined, creating a gap in AML coverage. Add monitoring scenarios for inbound wires, including amount, frequency and split‑deposit patterns.","CV3":"Money‑order deposits into the bank are not monitored – 0 % of £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions were checked. This leaves £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers unchecked, increasing the risk of missed suspicious activity. Add monitoring scenarios for money‑order deposits, covering amount, frequency and split‑deposit patterns.","AD1":"The advisory for multiple credit‑card repayments to many individuals is not being triggered – only a transaction‑count rule is applied, so only 3 of the 25 matching customers have a case. This leaves 22 customers, representing £2,115,842, unflagged despite 12 % of the cohort normally generating cases, increasing AML risk. Introduce a scenario that flags multiple credit‑card repayments to ten or more different individuals as described in the advisory.","AD2":"The advisory for multiple money orders deposited on the same day below £2,500 is not being triggered – only 2 of the 25 matching customers have a case. As a result, £668,454 associated with 8 % of the cohort remains unmonitored, exposing the bank to potential structuring. Add a scenario that flags several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500, as outlined in the advisory.","BL1":"Fifty unflagged customers rank among the most unusual of the 43,927 customers with no case, with money‑in amounts such as £607,808 and £831,312 placing them in the top 0.1 % and high‑risk‑country transaction counts of 17‑22 in the top 0.5‑0.7 %. Their combined unusual behaviour indicates a significant residual risk. Send these customers for manual review, beginning with the highest‑ranked individual.","BL2":"Customers scoring 32‑39 have a 1.8 % rate of highly unusual behaviour, compared with only 0.4 % for those scoring 40‑48. The current 40‑point threshold therefore excludes a group that is more suspicious than many who are allowed through, creating a blind spot. Lower the case threshold or regularly sample scores 32‑39 for review.","BL3":"Nineteen of the 25 customers suppressed by the valued‑client list sit in the top 2 % of most unusual activity. Because suppression prevents any case, even the two who have already reached case‑scoring levels remain invisible, undermining risk management. Remove automatic suppression and treat valued clients like any other customer for case generation.","CV4":"Credit‑card repayments out are only assessed by a transaction‑count rule (M03_outbound_velocity), covering £63,913,161. The rule ignores payment amounts, countries and counterparties, so potentially risky repayments are not evaluated. Add amount and counterparty criteria to the credit‑card repayment checks.","CA1":"The M01_outbound_high_risk rule assigns 5 points but is correct in only 5.1 % of the 2,379 reviewed cases. With a false‑alarm rate of roughly 95 %, the rule inflates the risk score without adding real detection value. Reduce its weight from 5 to about 2 points.","CA2":"M02_large_outbound carries 5 points yet is accurate in only 5.5 % of the 5,418 reviewed cases. The high false‑alarm rate means it contributes unnecessary points to many customers. Adjust its weight down to around 2 points.","CA3":"M03_outbound_velocity awards 10 points but is correct in only 10.1 % of the 2,881 reviewed instances. Its large point value generates many false alerts, diluting the effectiveness of the scoring model. Lower its weight to roughly 4 points."}}
